items.message: `php` detection treats a malformed or empty `composer.json` as no PHP stack, silently.
The `rake_test` guard requires a `Gemfile`, so a Rakefile-only repository never binds `bundle exec rake test` even when the Rakefile defines the task.
`cmake --build build` is bound for any `CMakeLists.txt`, but `build/` is only the conventional directory; the configure step is not run, so the build will fail on a fresh tree.
`dotnet restore` is unconditionally appended to `provision_commands` whenever `dotnet` is true, running before other provision steps with no guard.
The Rakefile-only negative case asserts `test_command == ()` but does not assert what the decline says, leaving the `STACK_HINTS` path untested for the no-Gemfile case.

1 finding(s) kept without a line: src/in_lockstep/lockstep.py:522 points outside every hunk this change produced in that file. The claim may still be right, so it is reported; the coordinate is not, so it is not.
One-level-down scan calls `manifest_present` (which may `glob`) for every entry in `BUILD_MANIFESTS` for every subdirectory iterated.
Regex applied to Rakefile content with re.MULTILINE but no size or content limit before the match.
composer.json is parsed with json.loads on the full file content with no size limit.

1 finding(s) kept without a line: src/in_lockstep/lockstep.py:524 points outside every hunk this change produced in that file. The claim may still be right, so it is reported; the coordinate is not, so it is not.
Declined-message assertion for CMake without `enable_testing()` is too weak to catch a regression.
One-level-down test does not assert that glob entries (`*.csproj`) are found, only that the formatted string `api/*.csproj` appears in the decline.
No test covers a Rakefile-only repository (no Gemfile) reaching a non-empty test command.
